title: U.N. "Reboot the Earth" Hackathon
location: Peter J. Shields Library at UC Davis, 167
description:
In partnership with the United Nations, the UC Davis Open Source Program Office (OSPO)  and DataLab will host a "Reboot the Earth" hackathon. Reboot the Earth is a global initiative that addresses local climate and environmental challenges through open source solutions. 

Representatives of local agencies championing each challenge track will serve as subject matter experts; students will also have access to mentors.

 

Who: 

The event is hosted by DataLab and the UC Davis Library, and is open to students of all backgrounds and experience levels, from any university or college. No prior hackathon experience is required—just curiosity and an eagerness to build something that matters. Participants are strongly encouraged to form interdisciplinary teams and include peers from a variety of majors. Each team may have a maximum of five people and has to include at least one UC Davis student.

 

Why:

Contribute to solving a problem in your community

Get experience working on a cross-functional team

Release an open-source productThe winners are invited to UN Open Source Week at United Nations Headquarters in New York! Travel expenses will be covered for the winning team. 

Schedule:

Kickoff Day (October 23)Wrap-up and Judging (October 24) Participation is required for at least part of both days.

 

Learn More:

At UC Santa Cruz's hackathon in November 2025, the winning team, FireForm, built an AI-powered voice-to-text tool that lets firefighters complete required documentation by speaking naturally instead of typing. They continued developing it after the event, and it has since been certified as a United Nations Digital Public Good. 

 

At UC San Diego (May 2026), the winning team created FireLink, an SMS-based platform that delivers wildfire updates to residents with no internet or smartphone required.

 

This Open Access Week event underlines the UC Davis Library’s commitment to open science.

title: Out of Line: Art at the Edge
location: Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis, 254 Old Davis Road, Davis, California, 95616
description:
Inspired by conceptual artist Bruce Nauman’s video work “Dance or Exercise on the Perimeter of a Square (Square Dance), 1967–68,” this exhibition explores Davis as a site of both artistic practice and political protest. 
Mike Henderson, Ester Hernandez, Malaquías Montoya, Bruce Nauman, Nancy Rubins, Dorothy Wiley and the student artists of UC Davis’ Third World Forum engage with film, print and performance to confront who they were and what their work meant in a world of radical change. They made work wherever and however they could: in collaborative workshops, student newsrooms, kitchens and living rooms. 
While rooted in the politics of the late 20th century, “Out of Line” finds renewed meaning in the present day.

description: This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. title: Brawn, Brews & Brats: A Day of Work, Brotherhood, and Courage
location: Galileo Place, 1909 Galileo Place, Suite C, Davis, CA, 95618, United States
description:
YoloCares Hosts Regional Gathering for Men and Boys Focused on Healing, Mentorship, and Community Service 
  
Davis, CA — In partnership with the Sutter Health Foundation, YoloCares’ Center for Loss & Hope will host Brawn, Brews & Brats: A Day of Work, Brotherhood, and Courage on October 24, 2026, bringing together men, teens, and boys from across the region for a unique community-based mental health initiative centered on grief, mentorship, and service. 
Participants from the organization’s GriefWise men’s gatherings, youth GriefBall camps, and Grief Ranch programs will spend the afternoon completing public service projects before gathering for a shared meal and closing reflection ritual. 
The event reflects a growing recognition that unprocessed grief often appears as anger, isolation, or violence among men and boys. By combining physical work, intergenerational mentorship, and structured reflection, YoloCares aims to offer a healthier pathway. 
“Many young men are taught to carry pain alone,” says Dr. Chris Erdman, Director of the Center for Loss & Hope. “This day shows another possibility — that strength can mean building something together, speaking honestly about the pain we carry, and committing ourselves to be a creative force for good in our communities and families.” 
The event aligns with statewide efforts to address the mental health needs of men and boys through connection, mentorship, and community engagement. 
Brawn, Brews & Brats is not a clinical program but a public demonstration of an emerging model: transforming grief into belonging and responsibility through shared labor and ritual. 
For more information: Dr. Chris Erdman, Director, The Center for Loss & Hope atYoloCares, cerdman@yolocares.org or generally at griefsupport@yolocares.org.

title: Author Talk: Market Memories Cookbook with Ann M. Evans & Georgeanne Brennan (Davis)
location: Blanchard Room, Mary L Stephens Davis Branch Library
description:
The cookbook, which has 92 recipes, arranged by season, also tells the story of how the county’s iconic market evolved as the brainchild of four young Davis people, including co-author Ann M. Evans, with a few farmers selling fruits and vegetables from the back of their pick-ups, to one of the most recognized farmers market in the United States. 

The story is told through personal essays by the co-founders and others with seminal involvement, 32 anecdotal quotes from vendors, shoppers, and elected officials, and a timeline chronicling market highlights over 50 years, as well as an in- memoriam page, commemorating the market vendors who are deceased.

The book is illustrated by Ann and Georgeanne as well, with beautiful pen and ink and watercolor washes for fruit and vegetables and flowers in all the seasons.

location: Robert Mondavi Institute - Sensory Building, Sensory Theater
description:
Join us for this quarter's Savor event: Fresh Starts: How California Farmers Markets Changed the Way We Eat.
 

The formation of the Davis Farmers Market 50 years ago was a revolutionary movement to connect consumers directly to farmers and helped shape the fresh flavors of California cuisine. Markets have been a cornerstone of the community and have also played a pivotal role in food access, especially during supply chain shortages and widespread food recalls. Inevitably, markets have evolved. Join us as we explore the history, impact and changing role of farmers markets in local communities. 

The event will feature a panel of leading industry experts including:
 

Ann Evans, UC Davis alumna, co-founder of the Davis Farmers Market and Davis Food Co-op, author and former mayor and city council member of the City of DavisSam Greenlee, chief executive officer of Alchemist Community Development CorporationChutharat Sae Tong, co-owner of Majka Pizzeria and Bakery in SacramentoModerator Catherine Brinkley, associate professor in Human Ecology, Community and Regional Development at UC Davis 

A pop-up exhibit from the library's Archives and Special Collections will be on display.

 

The event includes a welcome reception, a hosted bar and appetizers. Tickets are $25/person ($15/students). 

 

The Savor lecture series is a collaboration between the Robert Mondavi Institute for Wine and Food Science and the UC Davis Library.

For one day, we open our doors wide to celebrate and uplift the many cultures and people who make our region so vibrant. Explore cultural and artisan booths throughout I-House, enjoy food trucks out front, and experience a full lineup of performances on our backyard stage. It’s an open house in the truest sense: for the day, this is your house too, and every culture and community has a place here. 
I-Fest is a celebration, but your participation also supports the work I-House does all year long: welcoming newcomers, supporting English learners, and helping people from around the world find connection and community in Davis. At a time when many of us are feeling anxious or disconnected, creating spaces for joy, belonging, and connection feels more important than ever. Come celebrate cultures, meet new people, share in the joy, and experience what makes our community so special. 
For one day, I-House is your house. Come be part of it.

title: Let's talk about Female Sexuality & Fluidity
description:
Iama Embodied Community
If you have ever questioned your sexuality, experienced unexpected attraction, fallen for someone who challenged how you understood your sexual identity, or simply wondered why we don’t talk more openly about women’s sexuality, this event is for you.

I thought I was heterosexual until I fell in love with a woman. Reading Sexual Fluidity by Lisa Diamond has helped me make sense of my experience, and it made me realize how many women might be navigating similar questions without having a safe space to talk about them.

Come join us in a frank, open conversation and connect with other women with similar experiences. Let's talk about sexual fluidity and unexpected attraction, questioning or rethinking the labels we’ve used to understand ourselves, dating patterns, desire, and the ways our experiences of attraction may change, sexual shame, social expectations, and the messages we’ve inherited about sexuality, gender, identity, and giving ourselves permission to explore without needing all the answers (and labels), what else is on YOUR mind??

We’ll meet at Betty on T, they have coffee, tea, wine, and food options. Depending on our group size and the weather we’ll find a spot indoors or on the heated patio. I’ll have a sign on our table. Please RSVP to help with the reservation.

If you know a woman who might appreciate this kind of space, please share the event with her. You never know who might be looking for this conversation.

**About the hostess**

I’m Rola (pronounced Ru-lah), I am a pastor, yoga instructor, somatic guide, and trauma-informed facilitator currently working toward becoming a somatic coach. I bring experience in group facilitation, integrative somatic trauma therapy, embodiment, and a deep curiosity about the ways we experience ourselves and relate to one another.

**P.S.**

* This isn’t a formal workshop or a lecture. I’ll bring a few prompts to get the conversation started, but my hope is that it unfolds organically, shaped who shows up and what we feel moved to share
* There is no pressure to disclose anything personal, you are welcome to share, ask questions, or simply listen or be present
* You don’t need to be questioning your sexuality or have a particular identity to join. Even if you’re just curious about female sexuality and how it unfolds, you are welcome
* This space is for female-bodied individuals

title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.

title: Freedom of Expression at UC Davis: Know Your Rights
description:
Ever wondered where the line is between free speech, campus policy, and taking a stand? Whether you're planning a demonstration, organizing an event with your RSO, or just navigating lively debates around campus, knowing your rightsis key.

Join CSI's Assistant Director for Student Expression, Jose Napoles, for an interactive breakdown of what Freedom of Expression actually looks like on campus. We’ll clear up the confusion around campus forums, break down time, place, and manner policies, and give you the tools to make informed decisions and keep your communities safe.

In this session, you’ll learn how to:

Know Your Forums: Understand the difference between public, limited, and nonpublic spaces on campus and how your rights shift in each.

Decode Campus Policies: Get the real scoop on policy boundaries like amplified sound, tabling, and event security so your events run smoothly.

Protect & Advocate: Discover how the Student Affairs Response Team supports student expression, helps de-escalate tension, and connects you with key campus resources.

Navigate Real Scenarios: Work through practical examples of campus dissent and learn proactive strategies for community safety and self-care.

Who should attend? Student organization leaders, campus advocates, and any Aggie who wants to speak up, stay informed, and make an impact effectively.

Bring your questions and come learn more about Freedom of Expression at UC Davis.

*SPACE IS LIMITED!*

title: Un-Coding AI in the Classroom: 2-Day Workshop for Faculty and Instructors
location: DataLab Classroom, Shields Library, 360
description:
Generative AI is reshaping the landscape of higher education, raising important questions for teaching, learning, and academic integrity. Designed for faculty and instructors across all disciplines and requiring no prior technical background, this two-day workshop unpacks genAI and offers practical strategies for the university classroom. Whether you are curious about how these models work, eager to integrate AI into your teaching, or cautious about its impact on student learning, this series offers a supportive, nuanced space to explore. Participants will gain a clear foundational understanding of large language models (LLMs), evaluate the opportunities and limitations of genAI, and engage in hands-on practice configuring customized and privacy-protected AI learning environments for their courses.

 

The workshop runs Thursday-Friday December 10-11 from 9 AM - 4 PM daily with a break for lunch. Full participation in both days is recommended as topics build across sessions.

 

Day 1: Un-coding AI

Day 1 strips away the technical jargon to examine what genAI actually is — and what it isn't. Taking a no-code approach, we begin by exploring how LLMs process and generate language using intuitive, non-mathematical concepts. We examine how these models are developed and generate responses, explore the root causes of hallucinations, trace the influence of algorithmic bias, and discuss the impacts of genAI on the environment, society and self. 

 

Moving into practical engagement, we will discuss pedagogical and prompting strategies that keep human judgment and critical thinking firmly at the center of the learning process while safeguarding privacy. At the end of the day we will review institutional technology stack options (including the RockyAI implementation in Canvas, Google Gemini, and open-source models) to help you weigh the pros, cons, and privacy considerations as you build a practical roadmap for considering genAI integration into your courses.

 

Day 2: AI in the Classroom

Building on Day 1's foundational concepts, Day 2 transitions into an interactive, hands-on workshop focused on implementing privacy-protected AI tools directly into your curriculum. Participants will work step-by-step to configure course-ready environments on their own devices. We will explore an implementation of RockyAI embedded within Canvas for 24/7 student support grounded in instructor-approved course materials, set up local open-source models via Ollama to ensure complete data privacy and minimal environmental resource impact, and finally how to leverage the campus-licensed Google Gemini suite. By the end of this session, you will have functional AI tools set up for your courses along with the knowledge and confidence to guide your students in using them effectively to enhance their learning.

 

By participating in both days of this workshop, faculty and instructors will be able to:

Demystify Core Concepts: Explain the basic principles, capabilities, and limitations of large language models without relying on technical or mathematical jargon.

Validate & Evaluate Outputs: Apply systematic validation strategies to detect and explore hallucinations, bias, and factual inaccuracies in AI-generated content.

Articulate Impacts: Describe the environmental, social, cognitive and psychological impacts of genAI use and common teaching and learning pitfalls.

Navigate Campus Tech Stacks: Evaluate the privacy protections, costs, and practical trade-offs of various AI environments (including Canvas integrations, enterprise suites, and local models).

Deploy Privacy-Protected Tools: Configure and manage course-specific, privacy-focused AI assistants (such as Rocky AI, Google Gemini, and Ollama) to support student learning.

Design Pedagogy: Develop practical course-based roadmaps and effective prompting strategy examples to promote your student’s cognition, critical thinking, and academic integrity while protecting personal and institutional data.
 

Participants should bring their laptops* and charger. Bringing a reusable cup or water bottle is encouraged. Coffe, tea, and lunch is available for those who register in advance.

*Full participation in Day 2's activities requires that participants have permissions to install and run software locally on their laptop.

 

Questions? Contact us at datalab@ucdavis.edu.
